about.title: Union City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Union City never think about who made the space heater in the spare room, the tires on the car they drive down Alvarado Niles Road, or the ladder in the garage. You only start asking those questions after something breaks and someone gets hurt. That is where a product liability claim begins. Under California law, these cases usually rest on strict liability. Put simply, you generally do not have to prove the company was careless. What matters is whether the product had a defect in its design, in how that particular unit was manufactured, or in the warnings and instructions that came with it, and whether that defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach beyond the manufacturer to the distributor and the retailer that sold it to you. Tell us what happened, and our team will review your Alameda County product claim on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Union City Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict Liability Works in Your Favor
items.desc: California generally does not ask you to prove the manufacturer was negligent. Showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury is usually the heart of the case, and we can explain how that applies to your situation.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Evidence
items.desc: Do not throw away, repair, or return the item that hurt you, and hold onto the packaging, receipt, and any instructions. Our team can help arrange for it to be examined and preserved properly.

items.title: More Than One Company May Be Responsible
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the store that sold the product can all carry liability under California law. We'll work with you to sort out which parties belong in your claim.

items.question: My airbag didn't deploy in a crash on I-880 near Union City. Could that be a product liability case?
items.answer: It might be. Union City recorded 179 injury collisions in 2025, and when a safety component fails during one of those crashes, the injuries can be more serious than the collision alone would have caused. A defective airbag, seatbelt, or brake system can support a product claim separate from any claim against another driver. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until we've had a chance to look at it.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was faulty?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability commonly runs on strict liability, so the focus is on whether a design, manufacturing, or warning defect existed and whether it caused your injury. The company's state of mind is usually not the deciding factor. We can walk you through what evidence tends to matter most.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free case reviews, and we handle product liability claims on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
